findings.statement: OAuth apps can be account-level (managed by admins across the account) or user-managed (added individually by each user); the management type affects which scopes are available.
findings.excerpt: account-level app) or by users individually (user-managed app)

findings.statement: External apps intended for public Marketplace listing go through Zoom's review process before publication; internal-only apps don't require the standard Marketplace review.
findings.excerpt: after it passes Zoom's review process

findings.statement: Zoom runs a one-time domain verification to confirm you own the domains used for your Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, OAuth redirect, webhook callback, and home URLs.
findings.excerpt: We perform a one-time verification to make sure that the domain where you receive Zoom callbacks is owned by you.

findings.statement: Before submitting, provide reviewer release notes with a test plan and a populated test account with credentials for every user role your app supports.

Approval for an Authorization URL requires extra security evidence (SSDLC documentation, SAST and DAST scan results, a privacy policy, plus three of five further security documents); standard Marketplace publication does not require this extra package.
findings.excerpt: Custom-written summaries are not accepted as scan evidence.

findings.statement: Apps must support TLS 1.2 or higher and are expected to follow ongoing secure-SDLC practices: regular SAST/DAST scanning and periodic penetration testing.
Each requested scope needs a written justification, and adding a scope submits a request to Zoom's Security Review team, which may reject scopes it finds unnecessary.

Account-level or admin scopes require authorization by a user with matching admin Role Permissions, and an account may require a Marketplace admin to pre-approve the app before any user can authorize it.
findings.excerpt: Account-level scopes require an admin with the right permissions.

findings.statement: A Beta/Shareable URL reportedly lets up to about 10 external users install and test an app before it's published; without one, the app works only for accounts in the developer's own Zoom org.
findings.sourceTitle: How can I allow multiple users to test my Zoom OAuth app in development mode

findings.statement: Zoom staff described a roughly 72-hour initial-response SLA (excluding weekends and holidays), with the security-review stage alone taking up to about two weeks.
findings.sourceTitle: Marketplace App Production Approval Timelines Post Updates
findings.excerpt: our SLA is 72hours, not including weekends, US Holidays, and Company closings

findings.statement: One developer's app, flagged for extra review due to its technology, was still unresolved about seven weeks after resubmission.
findings.sourceTitle: Zoom App submitted on 4/5 and still no reply

findings.statement: Developers report common rejection causes: incomplete test credentials or test plans, missing or non-actionable documentation links, incomplete branding or listing details, and a missing or broken deauthorization URL.
findings.sourceTitle: Why is my Application getting rejected?

findings.statement: Zoom can order a mandatory security re-review of an already-approved app; one developer reported their app was unpublished after failing such a re-review.
findings.sourceTitle: When is a re-review needed for published apps?

findings.statement: Composio's Zoom integration requires creating your own Zoom OAuth app and pointing its redirect URI at Composio's callback; Composio does not offer a pre-built managed app for Zoom.
When an update request changes an app's scopes, Zoom automatically emails existing subscribers to notify them of the change.
Published public apps must send a signed POST to a Deauthorization Notification Endpoint whenever a user deauthorizes the app; private apps and apps still in development don't send this notification.

Zoom's classic-scopes reference names every OAuth scope by name, including meeting:read, meeting:write, user:read, user:write, recording:read, recording:write, webinar:read, webinar:write, report:read:admin, phone:read, phone:write, chat:read, chat:write, account:read:admin, account:write:admin, calendar:read, and calendar:write, each with its own one-line description.

claim.text: App creation goes through a fully self-serve build flow and standard Marketplace review, with no partner program or vetting step mentioned anywhere in the registration or review docs.
Every scope request goes to a dedicated Security Review team, and the standard review process includes a security-review stage that alone can take up to two weeks.
Public apps must pass Zoom's Marketplace review before they can be listed and connect real user accounts.
Account-level and admin-scoped access requires an admin with matching Role Permissions, and the account may require pre-approval by a Marketplace admin first.
A Beta/Shareable URL reportedly caps pre-publish testing at about 10 external users.

tierReason.text: Every scope request goes through a dedicated Security Review team, and the standard review process includes a security-review stage that alone can take up to two weeks before an app can go live.

claim.text: Zoom staff describe a roughly 72-hour initial-response SLA, with the security-review stage alone taking up to about two weeks (roughly 10 business days) before a decision.
Composio's Zoom integration has you create and register your own Zoom OAuth app rather than offering a pre-built managed one.

flow.text: A developer registers an app as account-level (admin-managed) or user-managed, requests scopes with written justifications, and the user is redirected to Zoom to grant consent.

appTypes.text: Account-level apps are managed by admins and can request admin-scoped data across the account; user-managed apps are limited to data the installing user can access.

tokenNotes.text: Published public apps must notify a Deauthorization Notification Endpoint whenever a user revokes access; private or in-development apps don't send this notification.

claim.text: meeting:read lets an app view the authorizing user's meetings; every scope, including this one, goes through Zoom's Security Review team.

scopes.neededFor: Creating or editing a user's own meetings.

claim.text: meeting:write lets an app view and manage the authorizing user's meetings, subject to Zoom's Security Review.
user:read lets an app view the authorizing user's own profile information.

scopes.allows: View and manage your own user information.

claim.text: user:write lets an app view and manage the authorizing user's own profile information.
recording:read lets an app access the authorizing user's own cloud recordings.
recording:write lets an app view and manage the authorizing user's own cloud recordings.

scopes.allows: Read-only access to your own webinars.

claim.text: webinar:read gives read-only access to the authorizing user's own webinars.

scopes.allows: Read and modify your own webinars.
scopes.neededFor: Creating or editing a user's webinars.

claim.text: webinar:write lets an app read and modify the authorizing user's own webinars.

scopes.neededFor: Admin-level reporting across the whole account.

claim.text: report:read:admin lets an app access account-wide report data, and requires an authorizing user with matching admin Role Permissions.

scopes.neededFor: Reading a user's Zoom Phone data.

claim.text: phone:read lets an app view the authorizing user's Zoom Phone information.

scopes.allows: View and manage your phone information.
scopes.neededFor: Managing a user's Zoom Phone data.

claim.text: phone:write lets an app view and manage the authorizing user's Zoom Phone information.

scopes.neededFor: Reading a user's chat messages and channels.

claim.text: chat:read lets an app view the authorizing user's chat message info.

scopes.neededFor: Sending or managing a user's chat messages.

claim.text: chat:write lets an app manage the authorizing user's chat message info.
account:read:admin lets an app view account-level info, and requires an authorizing admin.
account:write:admin lets an app view and manage account-level info, and requires an authorizing admin.
calendar:read lets an app view the authorizing user's calendar.

scopes.neededFor: Creating or editing a user's calendar events.

claim.text: calendar:write lets an app manage the authorizing user's calendar.

prerequisites.item: A published Privacy Policy and Terms of Use page, at a domain you can verify ownership of

claim.text: Zoom verifies ownership of the domains used for your Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, and callback URLs before approving the app.

prerequisites.item: Reviewer release notes with a test plan and a fully populated test account (one login per user role)

claim.text: Reviewers need release notes with a test plan and a populated test account covering every user role your app supports.

prerequisites.item: SSDLC documentation, SAST and DAST scan results (only if you need Authorization URL approval)

claim.text: Authorization URL approval needs SSDLC documentation and SAST/DAST scan results as supporting evidence, on top of standard Marketplace review.

steps.title: Found Zoom's developer portal and OAuth app build flow
steps.detail: The research stage located Zoom's app registration flow and its review and security-requirements pages.

claims.text: Zoom's OAuth app build flow is documented at developers.zoom.us.

steps.title: Create a Zoom developer account and register an OAuth app
steps.detail: Start a new app in the build flow and choose account-level or user-managed.

claims.text: Registering an app means picking account-level or user-managed, which affects which scopes you can request.

steps.title: Select your scopes and write a justification for each
steps.detail: Every scope needs a written reason; Zoom's Security Review team can reject scopes it finds unnecessary.

claims.text: Each requested scope needs a written justification and is reviewed by Zoom's Security Review team.

steps.title: Verify ownership of your redirect, privacy-policy, and terms domains
steps.detail: Zoom runs a one-time check (DNS TXT record, HTML file, or meta tag) before it will send callbacks to your domain.

claims.text: Zoom performs a one-time domain-ownership verification for your callback, privacy policy, and terms URLs.

steps.title: Build the deauthorization endpoint
steps.detail: Published public apps must accept a signed POST whenever a user deauthorizes the app.

claims.text: Published public apps must handle a signed POST to a Deauthorization Notification Endpoint.

steps.title: Populate a test account with credentials for every user role
steps.detail: Zoom's review team installs the production app into their own account and needs working test logins.

claims.text: Reviewers need a populated test account with a login for every user role your app supports.

steps.title: Draft your scope justification for the Security Review team
steps.detail: Use the Scope justification helper to prepare reviewer-facing notes for each scope you requested.

steps.title: Draft a reviewer test plan
steps.detail: Use the Reviewer test plan helper so Zoom's reviewer can exercise your integration quickly.

steps.title: If you need an Authorization URL, gather SSDLC/SAST/DAST security evidence
steps.detail: Authorization URL approval needs extra, specific evidence beyond standard Marketplace review.

claims.text: Authorization URL approval requires SSDLC documentation and SAST/DAST scan evidence beyond standard review.

steps.title: Submit for review and respond to any reviewer notes
steps.detail: Reviewer feedback appears as notes in your app's status panel; you must respond before resubmitting.

claims.text: Apps go through Zoom's review process, and reviewer notes must be acknowledged before resubmission.

steps.title: Approved and live
steps.detail: Once review passes, the app can connect real Zoom user accounts.

provider.who: Zoom's Marketplace Review Team, including a dedicated Security Review team for scopes
provider.what: Reviews functionality, branding, and every requested scope; the security-review stage alone can take up to about two weeks.

claims.text: Zoom's review covers functionality and scopes, with a security-review stage that can take up to two weeks.

customerAdmin.who: The Zoom account owner or an admin with matching Role Permissions
customerAdmin.what: Must authorize account-level or admin-scoped access, and the account may require the app to be pre-approved before any user can authorize it.

claims.text: Account-level and admin-scoped access needs an admin with matching Role Permissions, and the account may require pre-approval first.

endUser.what: Grants authorization at Zoom's consent screen; admin-scoped access still needs an admin, not just the user.

claims.text: Users grant authorization at Zoom's consent screen, though admin-scoped access additionally needs an admin.

stuckPoints.reason: Review stalls, or is rejected with an unclear reason
stuckPoints.fix: Check the Review Team's notes in your app's status panel (the speech-bubble icon) - you must acknowledge them before resubmitting.
stuckPoints.escalation: Reply on the review thread, or ask in the Zoom developer forum

claim.text: Developers report rejections for incomplete test credentials, missing documentation links, incomplete branding, or a missing deauthorization URL.

stuckPoints.reason: No reviewer response past the stated SLA
stuckPoints.fix: Follow up referencing your submission date and the 72-hour SLA; ask what stage the review is in.
stuckPoints.escalation: Reply on the review thread in the Zoom developer forum

claim.text: Zoom staff describe a 72-hour response SLA, but some developers have reported waits of many weeks in practice.

whileYouWait.text: A Beta/Shareable URL reportedly lets up to about 10 external users install and test your app before it's published.

keepsComingBack.text: Zoom can order a mandatory security re-review of an already-approved app, and a failed re-review can get the app unpublished.
